extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners (practitioners handling PCT national stage entry and ex parte reexamination)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for entering the U.S. national stage from an international (PCT) application (timing, translations, oaths/declarations, fees, sequence listings, abandonment) and the procedures/requirements for requesting and prosecuting ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely fulfillment of 35 U.S.C. 371 for national stage entry
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant in an international application must fulfill the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371 within the time periods set forth in paragraphs (b) and (c) of § 1.495 in order to prevent the abandonment of the international application as to the United States of America. The thirty-month time period set forth in paragraphs (b), (c), (d), (e) and (h) of this section may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International applications for which those requirements are timely fulfilled will enter the national stage and obtain an examination as to the patentability of the invention in the United States. Failure to comply results in abandonment as to the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration filing deadline for national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must file each required oath or declaration in compliance with § 1.63, or substitute statement in compliance with § 1.64, no later than the date on which the issue fee for the patent is paid. If notified that an oath/declaration has not been filed, the applicant must file it no later than the date on which the issue fee is paid to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time period is not extendable under § 1.136. The Office may dispense with prior notice if the required oath/declaration has been filed before the application is in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing fee & surcharge for late submissions entering national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of the processing fee set forth in § 1.492(i) is required for acceptance of an English translation later than the expiration of thirty months after the priority date. Payment of the surcharge set forth in § 1.492(h) is required for acceptance of any of the search fee, the examination fee, or the inventor’s oath or declaration after the date of the commencement of the national stage (§ 1.491(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late translations or late payment of specified fees require associated processing fees/surcharges to be accepted; these payments affect acceptance but do not extend statutory time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing translation requirements (pre/post July 1, 2022 distinction)
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications having an international filing date before July 1, 2022, a sequence listing need not be translated if it complies with PCT Rule 12.1(d) and the description complies with PCT Rule 5.2(b). For international applications having an international filing date on or after July 1, 2022, an English translation is required for any sequence listing in XML format ('Sequence Listing XML') containing non-English language values for any language-dependent free text qualifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must check the international filing date to determine translation obligations for sequence listings; noncompliant sequence listings may render parts canceled or require corrective filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing PCT Article 19 claim amendments by 30 months
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any amendments to the claims made under PCT Article 19, and a translation of those amendments into English, if they were made in another language, must be furnished not later than the expiration of thirty months from the priority date. Amendments under PCT Article 19 which are not received by the expiration of thirty months will be considered canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission of Article 19 amendments and translations is required to preserve those amendments in the U.S. national stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations of annexes to international preliminary examination reports
rubrics_metrics.description: A translation into English of any annexes to an international preliminary examination report (if applicable), if the annexes were made in another language, must be furnished not later than the expiration of thirty months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations not timely received may be submitted later with the processing fee specified in § 1.492(f); annexes for which translations are not timely received will be considered canceled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of non-English translations may be required
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification of the translation of the international application or any other document pertaining to an international application may be required where it is considered necessary if the international application or other document was filed in a language other than English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to supply verified translations when requested by the Office to establish accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of documents/fees as submission to enter national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The documents and fees submitted under paragraphs (b) and (c) of § 1.495 must be identified as a submission to enter the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371. If the documents and fees contain conflicting indications as between an application under 35 U.S.C. 111 and a submission to enter the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, the documents and fees will be treated as a submission to enter the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label submissions to avoid mischaracterization; when conflicting, Office treats them as national stage entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment rules for failure to meet national stage requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application becomes abandoned as to the United States thirty months from the priority date if the requirements of paragraph (b) of § 1.495 have not been complied with within thirty months from the priority date. If the requirements of paragraph (b) are complied with within thirty months but translations or the oath/declaration are not timely filed, the application will become abandoned as to the United States upon expiration of the time period set pursuant to paragraph (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thirty-month deadlines are firm; noncompliance leads to abandonment unless specified later time periods with fees are used where allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited amendment after national stage commencement (advancement out of turn)
rubrics_metrics.description: National stage applications having paid the search fee (§ 1.492(b)(1)) and examination fee (§ 1.492(c)(1)) may be amended after the date of commencement of national stage processing only to the extent necessary to eliminate objections as to form or to cancel rejected claims. Such national stage applications will be advanced out of turn for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive amendments after national stage commencement are restricted; paying fees and complying may result in priority advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: When inventor's oath/declaration required for national stage (35 U.S.C. 371(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant of an international application desires to enter the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 pursuant to § 1.495, and a declaration in compliance with § 1.63 has not been previously submitted in the international application, the applicant must file the inventor’s oath or declaration. The inventor, or each individual who is a joint inventor of a claimed invention, must execute an oath or declaration in accordance with the conditions and requirements of § 1.63, except as provided for in § 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether PCT declarations under PCT Rule 4.17(iv) satisfy US requirements; otherwise file US-compliant oaths or substitute statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form requirements for an oath/declaration (pre-AIA wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration must: (1) be executed in accordance with §§ 1.66 or 1.68; (2) identify the specification to which it is directed; (3) identify each inventor and the country of citizenship of each inventor; and (4) state that the person making the oath or declaration believes the named inventor(s) to be the original and first inventor(s) of the subject matter claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All actual inventors must make the oath except as provided in §§ 1.42, 1.43 or 1.47. If a non-inventor signs, the relationship and the facts 'upon information and belief' must be stated; legal representatives must state status and contact info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of PCT-filed oaths/declarations as complying with US requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration under § 1.63 will be accepted as complying with 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(4) if it complies with the requirements of §§ 1.63(a), (c) and (g). A substitute statement under § 1.64 will be accepted as complying if it complies with the requirements of §§ 1.64(b)(1), (c) and (e) and identifies the person executing the substitute statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a previously filed declaration suffices under § 1.63(d), submit a copy per § 1.63(d)(1) to comply with 371(c)(4). If it does not meet § 1.63/1.64, supplemental submissions (oath/declaration or ADS) will be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a new oath/declaration is required (changes after PCT filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new oath or declaration must be filed to satisfy 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(4) if the declaration was filed under PCT Rule 4.17(iv) and (1) there was a change in the international filing date pursuant to PCT Rule 20.5(c) after the declaration was executed; or (2) a change in the inventive entity was effected under PCT Rule 92 bis after the declaration was executed and no declaration by the changed inventive entity has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also required if priority claim corrected or added under PCT Rule 26 bis after the declaration was executed (then submit new oath/declaration or ADS identifying correct priority application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures when inventive entity changes during national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: If the oath/declaration filed pursuant to 371(c)(4) names a different inventive entity than the international application or if a change to the inventive entity was effected under PCT Rule 92 bis after execution, applicant must submit: (1) statements from persons added or deleted that any error occurred without deceptive intention; (2) processing fee (§ 1.17(i)); (3) written consent of assignee(s) if assignment executed; and (4) any new oath or declaration required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require other information as appropriate; follow petition provisions when correction of inventorship is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention election during national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner finds that a national stage application lacks unity of invention under § 1.475, the examiner may in an Office action require the applicant in the response to elect the invention to which the claims shall be restricted. Such requirement may be made before any action on the merits but may be made at any time before the final action at the discretion of the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of such requirement is provided under §§ 1.143 and 1.144.

rubrics_metrics.name: What may be submitted to patent file under § 1.501 (citations and written statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time during the period of enforceability of a patent, any person may file a written submission with the Office directed to: (1) prior art patents or printed publications believed to have a bearing on patentability of any claim; or (2) statements of the patent owner filed by the patent owner in a proceeding before a Federal court or the Office in which the patent owner took a position on the scope of any claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions under (2) must be accompanied by other documents/evidence and submitted in redacted form to exclude protected information. Submissions may be anonymous if identity is to be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation requirement for prior art submissions to be entered
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission under § 1.501 must include an explanation in writing of the pertinence and manner of applying any prior art submitted to at least one claim of the patent in order for the submission to become a part of the official file of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission is by the patent owner, it may include explanation of how the claims differ from any prior art submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service for non-owner citations
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission under § 1.501 by a person other than the patent owner must include a certification that a copy of the submission was served in its entirety upon the patent owner at the address provided in § 1.33(c). A submission that fails to include proper proof of service as required by § 1.248(b) will not be entered into the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service is mandatory for entry of third-party submissions into the patent file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay in entry of citations when reexamination pending
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination proceeding has been requested and is pending for the patent in which the submission is filed, entry of the submission into the official file of the patent is subject to the provisions of §§ 1.502 and 1.902; citations submitted after the date of an order to reexamine will be delayed until the reexamination proceeding has been concluded by issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of submission relative to reexamination affects when citations are entered into files; consult reexamination processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a request for ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for ex parte reexamination must include: (1) a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications; (2) identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested and a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every claim; (3) a copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon (with English translations of necessary parts); (4) a copy of the entire patent including front face, drawings, and specification/claims (double column format); (5) a certification that a copy of the request was served on the patent owner; and (6) a certification that statutory estoppel provisions do not prohibit the requester from filing the ex parte reexamination request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be accompanied by the fee set in § 1.20(c)(1). If incomplete, the requester will be notified and given opportunity to complete; failure results in no filing date and placement of the material in the file as a citation if it complies with § 1.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date for ex parte reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of the request for ex parte reexamination is the date on which the request satisfies all the requirements of § 1.510.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete requests do not receive a filing date until cured; be sure required parts, translations, certifications, and fee are submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney/agent filing on behalf of another must have authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is filed by an attorney or agent identifying another party on whose behalf the request is being filed, the attorney or agent must have a power of attorney from that party or be acting in a representative capacity pursuant to § 1.34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper authorization documentation is provided when an agent files for a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner determination standard for ex parte reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months following the filing date of a request for ex parte reexamination, an examiner will consider the request and determine whether or not a 'substantial new question of patentability' affecting any claim of the patent is raised by the request and the prior art cited therein, with or without consideration of other patents or printed publications. A statement and any accompanying information submitted pursuant to § 1.501(a)(2) will not be considered by the examiner when making a determination on the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination is based on the claims in effect at the time; notice of the determination is mailed to patent owner and requester. Where no SNQ is found, a portion of the fee is refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition/appeal opportunity after SNQ refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: The requester may seek review by a petition to the Director under § 1.181 within one month of the mailing date of the examiner’s determination refusing ex parte reexamination. Any such petition must comply with § 1.181(b). If no petition is timely filed or if the decision on petition affirms that no substantial new question has been raised, the determination shall be final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely petitions under § 1.181 are the only path to challenge a refusal to order reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-initiated ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director, at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent, may determine whether or not a substantial new question of patentability is raised by patents or printed publications discovered by the Director or brought to the Director’s attention, and may initiate ex parte reexamination without a request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally requests from outside the Office that the Director undertake reexamination on his own initiative will not be considered; determinations become part of the official file and are mailed to the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner statement timing and content in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in § 1.510(e), no statement or other response by the patent owner shall be filed prior to the determinations made in accordance with § 1.515 or § 1.520. The order for ex parte reexamination will set a period of not less than two months from the date of the order within which the patent owner may file a statement on the new question of patentability, including any proposed amendments. Any statement shall clearly point out why the subject matter as claimed is not anticipated or rendered obvious by the prior art patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Premature statements will not be considered and may be returned or discarded. If a third party requester exists, the patent owner’s statement must be served on the requester in accordance with § 1.248.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and formalities for proposed amendments in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed amendment is made by filing a paper directing specified changes to the patent specification (including claims) or drawings. Changes to the specification (other than claims and certain appendices) must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph (identify precise point). Changes to claims must include the entire text of each claim being changed and each new claim; parenthetical 'amended', 'twice amended' etc.; markings per paragraph (f). Drawings changes submitted as a sketch showing proposed changes in red for examiner approval; amended figures identified as 'Amended', new as 'New', canceled figures bracketed and 'Canceled.' Formal requirements are in § 1.52.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: status of all claims as of amendment date and explanation of support in disclosure must be supplied on separate pages. 'Large Tables', program listings, sequence listings have their own rule references for changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking conventions for amendments in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes relative to the patent being reexamined must include: (1) matter to be omitted enclosed in brackets; and (2) matter to be added underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow marking rules carefully so examiner can readily identify deletions and additions; claim amendments also require parenthetical amendment indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering and scope limitations during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered; numbering of any claims added must follow the highest numbered patent claim. No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent. Also, amendments are not effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proposed claim changes narrow or cancel claims, do not add new matter, and respect expiration limits; proposed amendments are treated as though entered during prosecution but become effective only upon issuance of certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When it appears the correct inventor(s) were not named, the Director may, on petition of all parties and satisfactory proof and payment of fee (§ 1.20(b)), or on order of a court, include in the reexamination certificate an amendment naming only the actual inventor(s). The petition must satisfy § 1.324 requirements. If reexamination concludes other than by a reexamination certificate, a certificate of correction indicating the change may be issued upon request by the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow petition requirements in § 1.324 and supply proof and fee; the Office may also require other information appropriate to the circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply rights of third-party requester during ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to the patent owner’s statement may be filed by the ex parte reexamination requester within two months from the date of service of the patent owner’s statement. Any reply must be served upon the patent owner in accordance with § 1.248. If the patent owner does not file a statement, no reply from the requester will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely service and adherence to the two-month period are required for the requester to have input after the patent owner’s statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of responses and refusal for late submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure to timely file or serve the documents set forth in § 1.530 or § 1.535 may result in their being refused consideration. No submissions other than the patent owner statement (§ 1.530) and the reply (§ 1.535) will be considered prior to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to service and filing deadlines or risk exclusion of material from consideration in the reexamination process.
